title: First jobs, new barriers
gist: A Resolution Foundation briefing for founders, technologists and investors finds young people without degrees face the hardest education-to-work transition, with unemployment around three times that of graduates, yet most career tech tools target graduates. It maps four stages of the transition where technology can or cannot credibly help.

insights.claim: In the UK, unemployment among young people qualified to GCSE level or below runs at around three times the rate for graduates, making non-graduates the group facing the steepest education-to-work transition.
insights.speaker: Aish Moothan
insights.so_what: Non-graduate youth are a large, underserved segment for employment and training services.

insights.claim: The education-to-work transition can be broken into four elements where technology may help: knowing options and reaching the right one, signalling ability and getting past screening, finding a first job that fits and lasts, and staying well and confident enough to see it through.
